- entire:what-happened: Explain why code looks the way it does by tracing the latest change for a file range or pasted snippet through `git blame` and deduplicated `entire explain` lookups. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. {"id":"ENT-1527","title":"CLI: compact output mode for `entire search --json` (agents pay ~10-30KB per result page)","description":"## Problem

`entire search --json` embeds each checkpoint's **full prompt** in every result, so a default page runs 10–36KB. For AI-agent consumers this is the dominant cost of using search:

* entire-search-bench measurements (Opus 4.6, single-repo, 100 runs/arm): the search arm read **more** input tokens than plain grep at equal turns (97K vs 79K in+cache mean, vocab-mismatch set; 70K vs 61K p50, keyword set) — the per-page JSON weight cancels out the turns that search saves.
* Skill arm traces: Claude Code persists 30–36KB tool outputs to disk and the agent then greps them back — extra wasted turns. Mitigated in the skill by defaulting to `--limit 5` (<pull-request id="e43706de-689d-43bf-88a5-46b803a911e5" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/review/search-skill-limit-guidance-repo-filter-disambiguation-earlier-code-7d23f17c2082">entireio/skills#39</pull-request>), but that just trades recall for weight.

## Request

A trimmed output mode, e.g. `--json --compact` (or `--fields id,repo,title,filesTouched,score`), that returns per hit only:

* `id`, `type`, `repo`, `branch`, `author`, `date`
* `filesTouched`
* rerank score
* a **truncated** prompt/title snippet (~200 chars), not the full prompt

Agents can fetch the full prompt for the one hit they care about via `checkpoint explain` (once <issue id="a9302907-2d8d-4e4b-b37e-ec8fec34311d" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1523/search-json-returns-checkpoint-ids-that-entire-checkpoint-explain">ENT-1523</issue> makes ids resolvable cross-repo).

## Expected impact

Search's turn advantage becomes a token advantage too: a 5-hit compact page should be ~1–2KB vs 10–36KB today. {"id":"ENT-1523","title":"search --json returns checkpoint ids that `entire checkpoint explain` cannot resolve (ULID vs 12-hex)","description":"## Symptom

`entire search --json` returns checkpoint results whose `data.id` format varies by source repo, and `entire checkpoint explain <id>` only resolves the 12-hex short form. The search→explain workflow (step 3 of the packaged `search` skill) breaks for the ULID ones.

Repro (CLI 0.9.0, 2026-08-05):

```
$ entire search "minRelevance reranker floor threshold" --json --repo '*' --limit 10
checkpoint 01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4 entire.io     <- ULID id
checkpoint 99fd2f6c0a4a                entire-search <- 12-hex id

$ entire checkpoint explain 01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4 --full --no-pager
no checkpoint or commit found matching "01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4"

$ entire checkpoint explain 99fd2f6c0a4a --no-pager
● Checkpoint 99fd2f6c0a4a ... (works)
```

## Impact

Observed live in the entire-search-bench `skill` arm: the agent picked the top cross-repo hit ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>) checkpoint), followed the skill's explain step, got "no checkpoint or commit found", and burned 3 turns retrying variants before answering from the snippet.

## Root cause (investigated 2026-08-05)

The ULID format is a red herring. The id format reflects the repo's checkpoint storage backend, and both are canonical:

* **Legacy branch backend** (`entire/checkpoints/v1`): 12-hex ids (entire-search).
* **Git-refs backend** (`refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`): 26-char Crockford ULIDs ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>)).

entire-search just passes the checkpoint's real id through (`internal/searcher/searcher.go:723`, from the `checkpoint_id` attr written in `internal/indexer/sink.go`). A git-refs checkpoint has **no 12-hex alias**, so "search returns the canonical short id" is not viable — nothing to fix server-side.

**Verified:** `entire checkpoint explain 01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4` **works** when run inside a checkout of [entire.io](<http://entire.io>) (the owning repo). The CLI's ID validation already accepts both formats (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id/id.go` — `KindOf`/`NewCheckpointID`).

The actual gap is **cross-repo resolution**: `checkpoint explain` only resolves against the cwd repo.

* `runExplainAuto` (`cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:461-524`) → `matchCheckpointPrefixWithRemoteFallback` (`cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go:196-244`): matches the local checkpoint store, then for a full ULID falls back to `FetchCheckpointRef` — which always fetches from the **current repo's** origin (`resolveCheckpointFetchTarget` in `git_operations.go`). A checkpoint from another repo can never resolve, regardless of id format (cross-repo 12-hex fails identically).
* `newExplainCheckpointLookup` (`explain.go:858-892`) opens only the cwd repository.
* The error message at `explain.go:503` ("no checkpoint or commit found matching %q") is what agents hit.

## Fix direction (agreed)

Add cross-repo support to `entire checkpoint explain` in the **CLI repo** (entireio/cli), via an explicit repo flag:

```
entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo <owner/name | gh/owner/name | ULID>
```

1. **Flag → repo identity**: reuse the CLI's existing repo-resolution machinery — `resolveRepoRef` (`cmd/entire/cli/resolveref.go:186`, core API) / the same accepted forms as `search --repo` (`resolveRepoFilters` in the search cmd handles `gh/owner/name`, bare `owner/name`, ULID). Do NOT hand-build GitHub URLs; resolve through the core repos APIs.
2. **Fetch the checkpoint ref from that repo's remote**: extend `FetchCheckpointRef` / `resolveCheckpointFetchTarget` to accept an explicit fetch target (URL or resolved repo) instead of always defaulting to the cwd origin. For git-refs ids the refspec is already built by `checkpoint.RefName(cid)` (`checkpoint/refs_naming.go:27-32`). Fetched objects land in the cwd repo's object store — acceptable.
3. **Bypass/scope the local lookup**: when `--repo` names a repo other than the cwd one, skip `matchCheckpointPrefix` against the local store and go straight to the remote fetch path.
4. **Wiring for agents**: `search --json` results already carry `org` + `repo` per checkpoint (`cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go:54-67`) — agents pass those straight into `--repo`. Update the packaged `search` skill (entireio/skills) to use the flag once shipped (follow-up to skills#39).

Scope notes:

* Primary target = git-refs (ULID) checkpoints, since per-checkpoint refs are cheap to fetch individually. Legacy 12-hex cross-repo (fetching another repo's `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch) can be supported the same way or explicitly rejected with a clear error — implementer's call, but the error must not be the generic "no checkpoint or commit found".

{"id":"ENT-1523","title":"search --json returns checkpoint ids that `entire checkpoint explain` cannot resolve (ULID vs 12-hex)","description":"## Symptom

`entire search --json` returns checkpoint results whose `data.id` format varies by source repo, and `entire checkpoint explain <id>` only resolves the 12-hex short form. The search→explain workflow (step 3 of the packaged `search` skill) breaks for the ULID ones.

Repro (CLI 0.9.0, 2026-08-05):

```
$ entire search "minRelevance reranker floor threshold" --json --repo '*' --limit 10
checkpoint 01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4 entire.io     <- ULID id
checkpoint 99fd2f6c0a4a                entire-search <- 12-hex id

$ entire checkpoint explain 01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4 --full --no-pager
no checkpoint or commit found matching "01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4"

$ entire checkpoint explain 99fd2f6c0a4a --no-pager
● Checkpoint 99fd2f6c0a4a ... (works)
```

## Impact

Observed live in the entire-search-bench `skill` arm: the agent picked the top cross-repo hit ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>) checkpoint), followed the skill's explain step, got "no checkpoint or commit found", and burned 3 turns retrying variants before answering from the snippet.

## Root cause (investigated 2026-08-05)

The ULID format is a red herring. The id format reflects the repo's checkpoint storage backend, and both are canonical:

* **Legacy branch backend** (`entire/checkpoints/v1`): 12-hex ids (entire-search).
* **Git-refs backend** (`refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`): 26-char Crockford ULIDs ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>)).

entire-search just passes the checkpoint's real id through (`internal/searcher/searcher.go:723`, from the `checkpoint_id` attr written in `internal/indexer/sink.go`). A git-refs checkpoint has **no 12-hex alias**, so "search returns the canonical short id" is not viable — nothing to fix server-side.

**Verified:** `entire checkpoint explain 01KYVBXNF3ZRG9CZ5YGNXYJCZ4` **works** when run inside a checkout of [entire.io](<http://entire.io>) (the owning repo). The CLI's ID validation already accepts both formats (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id/id.go` — `KindOf`/`NewCheckpointID`).

The actual gap is **cross-repo resolution**: `checkpoint explain` only resolves against the cwd repo.

* `runExplainAuto` (`cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:461-524`) → `matchCheckpointPrefixWithRemoteFallback` (`cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go:196-244`): matches the local checkpoint store, then for a full ULID falls back to `FetchCheckpointRef` — which always fetches from the **current repo's** origin (`resolveCheckpointFetchTarget` in `git_operations.go`). A checkpoint from another repo can never resolve, regardless of id format (cross-repo 12-hex fails identically).
* `newExplainCheckpointLookup` (`explain.go:858-892`) opens only the cwd repository.
* The error message at `explain.go:503` ("no checkpoint or commit found matching %q") is what agents hit.

## Fix direction (agreed)

Add cross-repo support to `entire checkpoint explain` in the **CLI repo** (entireio/cli), via an explicit repo flag:

```
entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo <owner/name | gh/owner/name | ULID>
```

1. **Flag → repo identity**: reuse the CLI's existing repo-resolution machinery — `resolveRepoRef` (`cmd/entire/cli/resolveref.go:186`, core API) / the same accepted forms as `search --repo` (`resolveRepoFilters` in the search cmd handles `gh/owner/name`, bare `owner/name`, ULID). Do NOT hand-build GitHub URLs; resolve through the core repos APIs.
2. **Fetch the checkpoint ref from that repo's remote**: extend `FetchCheckpointRef` / `resolveCheckpointFetchTarget` to accept an explicit fetch target (URL or resolved repo) instead of always defaulting to the cwd origin. For git-refs ids the refspec is already built by `checkpoint.RefName(cid)` (`checkpoint/refs_naming.go:27-32`). Fetched objects land in the cwd repo's object store — acceptable.
3. **Bypass/scope the local lookup**: when `--repo` names a repo other than the cwd one, skip `matchCheckpointPrefix` against the local store and go straight to the remote fetch path.
4. **Wiring for agents**: `search --json` results already carry `org` + `repo` per checkpoint (`cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go:54-67`) — agents pass those straight into `--repo`. Update the packaged `search` skill (entireio/skills) to use the flag once shipped (follow-up to skills#39).

Scope notes:

* Primary target = git-refs (ULID) checkpoints, since per-checkpoint refs are cheap to fetch individually. Legacy 12-hex cross-repo (fetching another repo's `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch) can be supported the same way or explicitly rejected with a clear error — implementer's call, but the error must not be the generic "no checkpoint or commit found".
* Without `--repo`, behavior is unchanged. With `--repo` matching the cwd repo, behave as today.
* Auth: fetching another repo's refs uses the same credentials as a normal git fetch of that repo; if the user lacks access, surface the git error clearly.

## Notes

* Interim mitigation shipped in the skill: <pull-request id="e43706de-689d-43bf-88a5-46b803a911e5" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/review/search-skill-limit-guidance-repo-filter-disambiguation-earlier-code-7d23f17c2082">entireio/skills#39</pull-request> tells agents not to retry and to answer from `prompt`/`filesTouched`.
* Considered and rejected: auto-fallback that queries the API for the owning repo on local miss (more magic, slower failure path); server-side id normalization (no 12-hex alias exists for git-refs checkpoints).","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1523/search-json-returns-checkpoint-ids-that-entire-checkpoint-explain","gitBranchName":"evis/ent-1523-search-json-returns-checkpoint-ids-that-entire-checkpoint","createdAt":"2026-08-06T00:57:50.886Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-07T05:11:49.468Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-08-07T05:11:49.453Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"In Review","statusType":"started","labels":["Bug"],"attachments":[{"id":"8577d6e4-3af6-482d-9ada-974b42c2303d","title":"Add cross-repo checkpoint explain via --repo (ENT-1523)","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1915"},{"id":"33338163-fe5d-4833-96c8-00e82b5374c8","title":"skills#39: search skill guidance fixes","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/entireio/skills/pull/39"}],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"8e117581-93c5-4ca8-b53b-8fc6d2c7510f","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-06T00:57:50.886Z","endedAt":"2026-08-07T05:11:49.461Z"},{"state":{"id":"03d080f4-4dc5-4a25-bc81-6797844f37c3","name":"In Review","type":"started"},"startedAt":"2026-08-07T05:11:49.461Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Evis Drenova","createdById":"bd1c458e-3bb3-4d0c-8ad7-e36f19afc156","team":"Entire","teamId":"832db0be-d9d8-45dc-9774-7f35babe62c0","relations":{"blocks":[],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"ENT-1528","title":"CLI: search click-tracking rider — search_id, impression log, explain-time correlation (agent CTR/MRR pipeline)"},{"id":"ENT-1527","title":"CLI: compact output mode for `entire search --json` (agents pay ~10-30KB per result page)"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

{"id":"ENT-1528","title":"CLI: search click-tracking rider — search_id, impression log, explain-time correlation (agent CTR/MRR pipeline)","description":"## Problem

~80% of search is expected to be agent-driven (especially in the CLI), and unlike web search we get no click signal: today `entire search --json` inlines full prompts, so there is never a second observable action after the results page. We can't compute CTR-by-position, MRR, or abandonment — the data that should drive ranking improvements.

<issue id="1c2e1d38-95a3-4a7e-9c86-33f5ef84deea" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1527/cli-compact-output-mode-for-entire-search-json-agents-pay-10-30kb-per">ENT-1527</issue> (compact output mode, shipped in <pull-request id="2f0200cf-6fed-433f-8c0e-37f87c67b4b8" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/review/add-compact-json-output-mode-to-entire-search-ent-1527-fba2923672c2">entireio/cli#1908</pull-request>) changes the structure: compact results carry only ids + snippets, so fetching full detail via `entire checkpoint explain <id>` becomes the mandatory second step. **That fetch is the click.** This issue is the small analytics rider that captures it. <issue id="a9302907-2d8d-4e4b-b37e-ec8fec34311d" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1523/search-json-returns-checkpoint-ids-that-entire-checkpoint-explain">ENT-1523</issue> (cross-repo resolvable checkpoint ids) makes those ids the "URL" the agent clicks.

Shipping this alongside compact-mode adoption matters: retrofitting the impression log later means losing the baseline ranking data from launch.

## Scope

1. `search_id` **on every search response** — a ULID in the JSON envelope (one line in the CLI; ideally minted by query-serve so server-side logs share the key). Log the impression set per search: `(search_id, query_hash, result_id, rank, score, match_type)`. Privacy: hash the query, never log raw query text or prompt content (matches the CLI's existing logging convention: operational metadata only).
2. **Explain-time correlation (zero agent cooperation — primary signal)** — CLI stores the last-N served `(search_id, result_id, rank)` tuples in session state (`.git/entire-sessions/` already exists for correlation). When `entire checkpoint explain <id>` runs and the id matches a recent impression in the same session, emit a click event through the existing `__send_analytics` path with `(search_id, result_id, rank, seconds_since_impression)`. Agents can't forget to do it and can't game it.
3. **Reformulation / abandonment signal (free)** — consecutive `search` calls in the same session with no intervening matched `explain` = abandonment at that ranking. Chains of reformulated queries ending in a click identify which query finally worked (also future training data for query rewriting).
4. **Fetch hint in compact output** — compact results (or the envelope) include a ready-made `explain: entire checkpoint explain <id>` hint so the click path is discoverable without requiring agents to plumb a `--search-id` flag (they would drop it inconsistently).

## Non-goals

* Explicit agent self-report (`--used <ids>` / MCP feedback param) — inconsistent and sycophantic; supplementary at best, separate issue if ever.
* Downstream conversion analysis (did searched-for files get edited in the eventual diff / transcript) — high-fidelity "purchase" signal unique to our transcript position, but an offline batch job over checkpoints; separate follow-up.

## Metrics unlocked

* CTR by rank position, MRR per query class
* Abandonment / reformulation rate per ranking
* Explain-rate per snippet length — tune the compact title cap (currently 200 runes) with entire-search-bench: too short → defensive multi-explains (noisy clicks), too long → no fetches (no clicks)
* Feeds the Search Dashboard in PostHog

## Caveats

* Agents batch tool calls and may fetch several results defensively. Also log repeat interactions with the same id (re-explains, follow-ups) to separate "opened top 3 defensively" from actual usefulness.
* Multi-agent / concurrent sessions: impression tuples must be session-scoped so clicks attribute to the right search.","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1528/cli-search-click-tracking-rider-search-id-impression-log-explain-time","gitBranchName":"evis/ent-1528-cli-search-click-tracking-rider-search_id-impression-log","createdAt":"2026-08-06T04:16:23.159Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-06T04:16:23.159Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"8e117581-93c5-4ca8-b53b-8fc6d2c7510f","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-06T04:16:23.159Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Evis Drenova","createdById":"bd1c458e-3bb3-4d0c-8ad7-e36f19afc156","team":"Entire","teamId":"832db0be-d9d8-45dc-9774-7f35babe62c0","relations":{"blocks":[],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"ENT-1527","title":"CLI: compact output mode for `entire search --json` (agents pay ~10-30KB per result page)"},{"id":"ENT-1523","title":"search --json returns checkpoint ids that `entire checkpoint explain` cannot resolve (ULID vs 12-hex)"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/evisdrenova/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.2.0/skills/writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

input.prompt:
In the repo /Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/cli/krakow (Go CLI, entireio/cli), map the `entire search` command flow in detail. Search breadth: thorough.

I need to add a `search_id` (ULID) to every search JSON response, and log an "impression set" per search: (search_id, query_hash, result_id, rank, score, match_type). Report:

1. `cmd/entire/cli/search_cmd.go` — the command's RunE flow: flags (esp. --json, --compact, --limit, --repo), where results are fetched (client/API call), and where JSON output is marshaled. Show the exact envelope struct(s) with field names and where they're populated (line refs).
2. `cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go` (and any other files in cmd/entire/cli/search/) — result types: what fields a result carries today (id, type, repo, branch, author, date, score, match_type, prompt/snippet, filesTouched...). Note exactly what compact mode emits per hit and any envelope-level fields.
3. Does the search server response already include any request/search id we could reuse? Check the API client structs the search command decodes into.
4. Where does compact mode put the `explain: entire checkpoint explain <id>` hint, if anywhere? (ENT-1528 wants a ready-made explain hint per result or in the envelope.)
5. Is there existing ULID generation in the repo (a package already used for ULIDs, e.g. oklog/ulid) — where and how is it used?
6. Any existing tests for search JSON output (search_cmd_test.go, search package tests) — file names and what patterns they use (golden output? struct assertions?).

Return: concise structured findings with exact file:line references, struct definitions verbatim for the JSON envelope and per-result types, and the compact-mode field list. No file dumps beyond the relevant structs.

input.description: Map analytics send path

In the repo /Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/cli/krakow (Go CLI, entireio/cli), map the analytics/telemetry infrastructure. Search breadth: thorough.

There is a hidden `__send_analytics` command.

2. The analytics package/API: how existing events are defined and emitted (event names, property maps, PostHog client?), where the telemetry opt-in/opt-out setting is checked, and 2-3 concrete examples of existing event emissions from commands (exact call sites with file:line).

4. Where does search or explain already emit analytics events today, if at all?
5. How events carry session/context identifiers today (session_id? machine id? repo id?) — field names used.

Return concise structured findings with exact file:line references and verbatim signatures of the emit function(s) I should call. No file dumps.

content.thinking:
With all three explorations complete, I'm ready to write the implementation plan to docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-ent-1528-search-click-tracking.md, starting with the scope from ENT-1528 including the search_id ULID in the JSON envelope.

I'm deciding to scope search_id to the semantic search full and compact JSON envelopes only, excluding the separate --code search path and TUI since the click funnel only applies to checkpoint results — keeping this lazy and focused rather than trying to cover every search response literally.

For impression logging, I'm thinking this should be an analytics event sent via the existing analytics pipeline, likely one event per search containing an array of impressions (search_id, query_hash, result_id, rank, score, match_type) rather than one event per result.

I'm also planning a local impression store for click correlation — a JSON file under the git common dir holding bounded recent impression tuples with timestamps, using file locking and atomic writes similar to existing patterns in the codebase, with some TTL or count-based cap to keep it small.

I want both the impression store writes and telemetry events gated behind the same telemetry-enabled check, so opted-out users get nothing written at all — better for privacy and avoids unnecessary disk writes.

For click correlation, I'm hooking into the explain paths (single-repo, cross-repo, and JSON export) through one shared helper that checks whether a resolved checkpoint ID matches a stored impression, also handling the case where the user typed a prefix or commit SHA directly.

I'm settling on matching either the original user-supplied target or the resolved full checkpoint ID against the impression's result_id, since commit SHAs resolve to a different checkpoint ID than what's stored in the impression. The click event itself just needs search_id and result_id — and since checkpoint IDs are opaque ULIDs with no meaning outside the repo, that's safe to emit without leaking anything sensitive.

For the query_hash field, I'm weighing plain sha256 against an HMAC keyed by machine ID — HMAC would prevent cross-user correlation but also kill the ability to group identical queries across users for ranking analysis, which seems like the actual goal here, so I'm leaning toward a straightforward sha256 of the normalized query text instead.

Now for the explain hint, I'm deciding to add it per-hit for checkpoint/commit/session result types but omit it for repo/pr types since those can't be explained, and I'll note that cross-repo explain via --repo now makes this hint more broadly useful.

I'm weighing envelope-level versus per-hit explain hints: a single envelope hint saves tokens, but per-hit exact commands are more reliable for agents to copy-paste correctly across repos, so I'm leaning toward per-hit hints despite the cost.

Reformulation detection can actually be free — PostHog can infer it offline from impression and click events without needing a dedicated event. But I could make it cheaper to analyze by tagging new search impressions with a `prev_search_id` when there's a recent unclicked search in the store, which means the click emitter needs to mark impressions as clicked so I know when a prior search went unanswered.

I should keep clicks un-deduplicated though, since the issue explicitly wants repeat interactions logged (re-explains), so I'll track a `click_seq` counter per impression rather than collapsing repeats. That keeps the scope modest: mark `clicked_at` on impressions, add `click_seq` to click events, and chain `prev_search_id`/`prev_clicked` on search events — all derivable without heavy new infrastructure.

Since PostHog can sessionize by distinct_id and timestamp, I don't strictly need explicit reformulation chaining, but sessionizing purely by machine-id+time risks conflating concurrent agents across different repos. Since we already read the store before writing, adding `prev_search_id` is cheap (~10 lines) and directly supports the "chains of reformulated queries" requirement, so I'll include it. Now I'm thinking through event naming conventions, building on the existing `cli_command` pattern.

I'll include session_id as a best-effort, possibly-empty property since impressions need to be session-scoped for attribution, joined by search_id and result_id. For storage, I'm designing a JSON structure at the git common dir path that tracks searches with their query hash, session id, timestamp, result impressions, and click counts.

I'm deciding `entire clean` doesn't need to touch this new directory since similar state already lives there uncleaned. For code organization, I'll follow the existing cli package conventions—putting tracking logic in a search_analytics.go file and telemetry builders in a dedicated search.go following the checkpoint_policy.go pattern, keeping the store accessible to both search and explain commands. Now I'm working through the wiring: where in search_cmd.go's RunE to mint the search_id and trigger telemetry after output is written.

I'll mint the search_id unconditionally before writing output, regardless of whether telemetry is enabled, so the output shape stays consistent—then if telemetry is on, record impressions from the actual emitted page and track the event. This requires either refactoring the JSON writers to return the emitted page data, or computing pagination separately in RunE rather than inside the writer functions as it currently works.

For the explain click tracking, I'm considering a helper that fires on successful checkpoint resolution across explain.go, explain_repo.go, and explain_export.go, but I need to be careful about double-firing in the commit fallback path—since runExplainCheckpointWithLookup gets re-entered with a trailer-derived checkpoint ID rather than the original user-supplied commit SHA, hooking inside that function would only see the resolved ID, not the original target.

Prefix matching is worth including since it's trivial with strings.HasPrefix, even though agents likely paste full ids. I'll simplify to a single helper function that records search clicks given the user's target and resolved checkpoint ID, then wire it into the call sites: after the lookup match in runExplainCheckpointWithLookup, after the summary resolution in explain_repo.go, and likely one more location.

I also need to hook this into runExplainExport after resolveExplainCheckpointID succeeds. There's a double-fire concern: if a user types a commit SHA that misses the auto-detection but resolves via commit trailer to a checkpoint ID, the helper fires with the commit SHA as userTarget, but if the original search impression was for the commit result rather than the checkpoint, it won't match — that's an acceptable limitation since commit hits are secondary. For the helper itself, I need to load the store, handle the case where the file is missing by returning early, and read with a shared flock to find a matching impression among recent searches, matching either the exact resolved ID or a prefix match when the target is at least 6 characters long.

On finding a match, I increment the click count, save the store, and track a click event with fields like search_id, result_id, rank, seconds_since_impression, click_seq, query_hash, session_id, score, and match_type — gated first by telemetry settings, though the store file's absence when telemetry is off naturally gates this too. Performance-wise this is negligible since it's just one small file read during an interactive explain run. For testing, since SpawnDetached is a no-op in tests, I'll focus on asserting build payloads and store round-trips, including tests for impression/click payload builders checking nil cases, shape, and that no raw query leaks, plus store record tests.

I also need to cover lookup, TTL expiry, capping, and click marking in the store, while skipping concurrency concerns. For search_cmd, I want the envelope to carry search_id from both writers, with explain hints shown per hit for checkpoint/commit but not repo/pr, and including --repo when cross-repo. I'll factor the click-matching logic into a testable helper that takes the store, target, resolved value, and current time, and returns the matched event fields. I also need a query hash helper that normalizes and truncates a sha256 hash. The --code path is out of scope since there's no explain funnel there, and full JSON output doesn't need per-result changes since impressions are computed directly from search results — the hint stays compact-mode-specific since full JSON already includes the whole prompt.

Now I'm deciding that search_id should appear in the envelope for both full JSON and compact output, since every search response should carry it. I'm sketching out the implementation plan as bite-sized TDD tasks: first, building the query hash and impression store with its types, recording/matching functions, TTL/cap logic, and file locking, placed in the CLI package since it needs access to the git common directory. Second, building the telemetry events module with structs and tracking functions for search performed and click events, following the existing checkpoint policy pattern. Third, wiring search_id minting and explain hints into the JSON writers in search_cmd.go.

Writers return emitted page info, then I need to wire impression recording into the search RunE path behind a telemetry gate, building impressions from the returned page and tracking search performed events with previous search_id chaining. Next comes click correlation in explain — a helper function wired into three call sites with tests for the matching logic. Finally, I'm considering whether documentation updates (the telemetry event inventory in docs/security-and-privacy.md) should be folded into the earlier tasks rather than treated as a separate step.

I'm deciding to fold the privacy doc update into the impression and click tasks, with one final verification task covering docs plus the check command. Since the plan needs real, executable code rather than placeholders, I'm working out exact constants and file names for the search impressions module.

Still defining data structures...

I'm working out the matching rule: for each search ordered newest first, check each result for equality against the resolved ID or target ID, falling back to a prefix match when the target is at least 12 characters long, since legacy hex IDs are exactly 12 characters while ULID prefixes can be longer.

I still need to verify the actual flock API used in pushqueue.go and trail_context_cache.go, the jsonutil helpers for atomic writes and indented marshaling, the LoadEntireSettings signature, and the Build/Track pattern in checkpoint_policy.go so the plan references real, working code rather than guesses.…

**How it works, end to end:**

1. **`search_id`** — minted client-side (ULID, crypto/rand) since the server response carries no request id and the CLI merges multiple cell responses. It goes into both JSON envelopes (full + compact) as `search_id`, always — it's response metadata, not telemetry.
2. **Impressions** — each served page yields `(result_id, rank, score, match_type)` tuples with absolute 1-based ranks. When telemetry is opted in, they're (a) sent as one `cli_search_performed` event through the existing detached `__send_analytics` pipeline, and (b) persisted to a flock-protected `search-impressions.json` under `.git/entire/` (1-hour TTL, last 20 searches), following the existing trail-cache/pushqueue patterns.
3. **Clicks** — `entire checkpoint explain` has exactly three id-resolution success points (prose, cross-repo, export); each gets a one-line hook that checks the store and emits `cli_search_result_clicked` with rank, `seconds_since_impression`, and `click_seq` (repeat explains counted, per the defensive-batch-fetch caveat in the issue). Zero agent cooperation needed.
4. **Reformulation** — each search event carries `prev_search_id` + `prev_search_clicked`, so abandonment chains are queryable in PostHog directly.
5. **The hint** — compact hits gain an `explain` field with the exact command, including `--repo org/name` for cross-repo checkpoint hits; omitted for repo/pr/session rows explain can't resolve.

**Decisions you may want to veto:** query privacy is a truncated SHA-256 of the normalized query (never raw text — new convention, none existed); `session_id` is best-effort via the most-recent-session heuristic (there's no env var identifying the agent session in subprocesses — correlation key is `search_id`+`result_id` instead); the `--code` path, TUI, and `entire clean` support for the new file are explicitly out of scope.

The plan has 6 TDD tasks with full test and implementation code. Two execution options:

1. **Subagent-driven (recommended)** — I dispatch a fresh subagent per task and review between tasks.
2. **Inline** — I execute the tasks in this session with checkpoints.

## Implementation plan (revised — stateless, privacy-max)

Scope trimmed per Evis: no local correlation state (nothing under `.git/entire*`), no impression tuples, no `seconds_since_impression`/rank/click-seq bookkeeping. Two flat, anonymous events, correlated later in PostHog (dashboard/MCP) by `distinct_id` + time. Goal: see which results agents run `explain` on, web-CTR-style, without a client-side metrics pipeline.

### What ships

**1. `search_id` in the JSON envelope (always — response metadata, not telemetry)**

`"explain": "entire checkpoint explain <id>"`, with `--repo <org>/<name>` appended for cross-repo checkpoint hits (works since #1942). Omitted for repo/pr/session rows explain can't resolve. This makes the fetch-detail step (the "click") copy-pasteable.

**3. Event `cli_search_performed`** — one per JSON search invocation:
`search_id`, `query_hash` (truncated SHA-256 of the normalized query — raw text never sent), `mode` (json|compact), `result_count`, `total`, `page`, `limit`, `cli_version`, `os`, `arch`.

`checkpoint_id` (opaque ULID/12-hex), `source` (prose | export | cross_repo), `cli_version`, `os`, `arch`.

## Telemetry

The CLI captures anonymous usage analytics by default. Sent to PostHog with `DisableGeoIP` enabled. Captured per command: command name, selected agent, whether Entire is enabled in the repo, CLI version, OS/arch, installed git version (best-effort; omitted if git is absent or unparseable), and **names** of flags passed (never their values). The distinct ID is a hashed machine identifier (`machineid.ProtectedID`), not a user identity.

Not captured: flag values, prompt text, transcripts, file paths, repository identifiers, GitHub usernames, source code.

Opt out via any one of:

- `--telemetry=false` on a command that accepts it.
- `"telemetry": false` in `.entire/settings.json` or `.entire/settings.local.json`.
- `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` in the environment.

## Reporting a vulnerability

For vulnerability disclosure, see [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) at the repo root: email `security@entire.io`, expect acknowledgment within 48 hours and resolution of criticals within 90 days.

Done — ENT-1528 is implemented, and the full CI suite passes (unit + integration + all 4 Vogon canary E2E tests, lint clean, gofmt clean).

**What was built** (the simplified, stateless design per your corrections — nothing written to `.git/entire*`, no impressions, no timing bookkeeping):

- **`search_id` in every search JSON envelope** — client-minted ULID, in both `--json` and `--compact` output (the server response has no request id and the CLI merges per-cell responses, so it must be minted client-side).
- **Per-hit `explain` hint in compact output** — `"explain": "entire checkpoint explain <id>"`, with `--repo org/name` appended for cross-repo checkpoint hits (rides PR #1942); omitted for repo/pr/session rows that explain can't resolve. This makes the "click" copy-pasteable for agents.
- **`cli_search_performed` event** — `search_id`, `query_hash` (truncated SHA-256 of the normalized query; raw text never sent), mode, result_count, total, page, limit.
- **`cli_checkpoint_explained` event** — the opaque checkpoint id plus which resolution path fired (`prose` / `export` / `cross_repo`), hooked once at each of explain's three id-resolution success points.
- Both events follow the existing `Build*Payload`/`Track*` pattern through the detached `__send_analytics` spawn, double-gated on `settings.Telemetry` + `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`. The search→explain funnel, reformulation/abandonment, and "which results get explained" all assemble in PostHog by `distinct_id` + time — no local state.

**Files:** new `telemetry/search.go` + `search_telemetry.go` (each with tests), edits to `search_cmd.go` (+9 new/updated tests), one-line hooks in `explain.go` / `explain_export.go` / `explain_repo.go`, and a telemetry section update in `docs/security-and-privacy.md`. ~170 insertions total.

The plan (revised to this scope) is posted as a comment on ENT-1528, and I've saved both memories: plans go to Linear tickets from now on, and CLI telemetry stays stateless/flat/privacy-max.

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --title "Add search_id, explain hints, and search relevance telemetry (ENT-1528)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Agent-driven search (~80% of expected search traffic) has no web-style click signal, so we can't tell whether the results we return are relevant. This closes the loop statelessly — no local correlation files, correlation happens in PostHog ([ENT-1528](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1528), full plan in the ticket comments).

- **`search_id` in every search JSON envelope** (`--json` and `--compact`): a client-minted ULID — the server response carries no request id and the CLI merges per-cell responses, so it can't come from the server. Also the future seam for server-side impression logging in query-serve.
- **Per-hit `explain` hint in `--compact` output**: `"explain": "entire checkpoint explain <id>"`, with `--repo <org>/<name>` appended for cross-repo checkpoint hits (rides #1942); omitted for repo/pr/session rows explain can't resolve. Makes the fetch-detail step copy-pasteable for agents.
- **`cli_search_performed` event**: `search_id`, `query_hash` (truncated SHA-256 of the normalized query — raw text never sent), mode, result_count, total, page, limit.
- **`cli_checkpoint_explained` event**: opaque checkpoint id + which resolution path fired (`prose` / `export` / `cross_repo`), hooked once at each of explain's three id-resolution success points.

The search→explain funnel (result relevance), reformulation/abandonment chains, and "which checkpoints get explained" are all queryable in PostHog by `distinct_id` + time — no client-side metrics pipeline.

## Privacy

No query text, prompts, file paths, repo names, or session ids in any event; nothing written locally. Both events follow the existing `Build*Payload`/`Track*` pattern through the detached `__send_analytics` spawn and are double-gated: `settings.Telemetry == true` at the call site + `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` inside `Track*`. Documented in `docs/security-and-privacy.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run fmt && mise run lint` — clean
- [x] `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + Vogon/roger-roger E2E canary) — all passed, on the rebased tree
- [x] New tests: payload shapes for both events (raw query/impressions/session_id asserted absent), query-hash normalization, ULID search_id, `search_id` in both envelopes, same-repo vs cross-repo explain hints, no hint on repo/pr rows, served-count returns

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
Here's the full flow, following one realistic exchange from an agent's question to a PostHog dashboard.

## The setup

Say a developer using Claude Code in the `entireio/cli` repo asks: *"why does checkpoint push only go to one remote?"* The agent decides to search prior work:

```bash
entire checkpoint search "checkpoint push remote election" --compact --limit 5
```

## Step 1 — Search serves results and mints the `search_id`

In `search_cmd.go`'s RunE, the query goes to query-serve, per-cell responses get merged, and because output is JSON, the CLI calls `newSearchID()` — a ULID minted client-side (the server response has no request id, and after the cross-cell merge there'd be no single server-side identity anyway). The agent sees:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "REDACTED",
      "type": "checkpoint",
      "repo": "entireio/cli",
      "branch": "main",
      "title": "Elect a single checkpoint sync remote instead of tracking-config tiers",
      "filesTouched": ["cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go"],
      "score": 0.91,
      "matchType": "semantic",
      "explain": "entire checkpoint explain REDACTED"
    },
    {
      "id": "REDACTED",
      "type": "checkpoint",
      "repo": "entirehq/entire.io",
      "title": "Handle fork setups where origin is unpushable",
      "score": 0.77,
      "matchType": "semantic",
      "explain": "entire checkpoint explain REDACTED --repo entirehq/entire.io"
    }
  ],
  "total": 2, "page": 1, "total_pages": 1, "limit": 5,
  "search_id": "REDACTED"
}
```

Two things in that payload do the work: compact mode withholds the full prompt (ENT-1527), so the agent *must* make a second call to get detail — and the `explain` field hands it that exact command, including `--repo` when the hit lives in another repo (riding the cross-repo explain from #1942). Repo/pr/session rows get no hint because explain can't resolve them.

## Step 2 — The impression event fires

Right after writing the output, RunE calls `emitSearchPerformed`. It checks the two gates — `settings.Telemetry == true` in `.entire/settings.json`, then `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` inside the tracker — and builds:

```json
{
  "event": "cli_search_performed",
  "distinct_id": "<HMAC-hashed machine id>",
  "properties": {
    "search_id": "REDACTED",
    "query_hash": "a3f81c20b9d4e576",
    "mode": "compact", "result_count": 2, "total": 2, "page": 1, "limit": 5,
    "cli_version": "0.9.2", "os": "darwin", "arch": "arm64"
  }
}
```

`query_hash` is a truncated SHA-256 of the lowercased, whitespace-collapsed query — the raw text never leaves the machine. Delivery is the existing fire-and-forget path: the payload is handed to a detached `entire __send_analytics <json>` child process that posts to PostHog, so search latency is untouched even if PostHog is slow.

## Step 3 — The agent "clicks"

The agent copies the hint for the top hit:

```bash
entire checkpoint explain REDACTED
```

Explain resolves the id through one of three paths, and each has exactly one emit at its resolution-success point:

- **prose** (what just ran): `runExplainCheckpointWithLookup`, the moment the prefix matches exactly one checkpoint
- **export** (`--json` / `--transcript`): inside `runExplainCheckpointJSON` / `runExplainStreamTranscript` — deliberately *not* in the shared resolver, because `entire checkpoint tokens` uses that resolver too (yesterday's Trail Review finding)
- **cross_repo** (`--repo entirehq/entire.io`): `runCrossRepoExplain`, after the cell read confirms the checkpoint exists

So a second event fires:

```json
{
  "event": "cli_checkpoint_explained",
  "properties": {
    "checkpoint_id": "REDACTED",
    "source": "prose",
    "cli_version": "0.9.2", "os": "darwin", "arch": "arm64"
  }
}
```

Note what the CLI *doesn't* do: no file written anywhere, no lookup of "was this id in a recent search," no rank math. It fires on every successful explain, unconditionally (modulo the telemetry gates).

## Step 4 — The funnel assembles in PostHog

Correlation happens entirely at query time, joining on `distinct_id` + timestamps:

- **Relevance / conversion**: a funnel of `cli_search_performed → cli_checkpoint_explained` within, say, 5 minutes on the same machine. High conversion = results worth fetching.
- **Reformulation / abandonment**: consecutive `cli_search_performed` events with no `cli_checkpoint_explained` between them = the ranking failed and the agent retyped the query. Distinct `query_hash` values in the chain show how many attempts it took.
- **What's actually useful**: group `cli_checkpoint_explained` by `checkpoint_id` — since the id is real (opaque, but real), you can pull those checkpoints internally and judge whether the "popular" results are genuinely relevant. `source: cross_repo` also tells you how often the cross-repo hint gets exercised.

## The accepted tradeoff

Because there's no local state, the search→explain link is *probabilistic* (same machine, close in time), not proven set-membership — and CTR-by-rank isn't measurable client-side. If that's ever needed, the seam is already in place: `search_id` sits in the envelope, so the next step would be sending it with the search request and logging impressions server-side in query-serve, where the result set is known anyway.

That's the whole machine: one ULID, one output field, two flat events — everything else is a PostHog query.

I'm thinking about whether deterministic search-to-explain linkage requires local state, which was previously ruled out for .git/entire folders—though maybe storing it elsewhere like XDG cache could honor the privacy-first spirit while still working.

A better option is embedding the search_id directly in the explain hint itself, making it stateless and deterministic: the hint becomes copy-pasteable with a hidden --search-id flag, so agents that copy it automatically carry the correlation while hand-typed commands fall back to time-based matching. This keeps things simple with no local state and no privacy leakage, since the search_id is opaque—though I'm weighing the token cost of adding this to every hint.

A more robust but heavier option is server-side impression logging, where the query-serve request logs (search_id, result_id, rank) and the explain event joins against those logs for deterministic click and rank data—but that requires server-side work and cross-system joins outside this repo. I'm leaning toward the CLI-side embedded search_id as the pragmatic choice since it directly measures the funnel we care about: agents using the hint as intended.

Since the flag is optional, fallback time-correlation still works if an agent omits it, and we can track hint-compliance rate as a metric. content.text:
Yes — and without violating your constraints (no local state, no server changes required). The trick is that **we author the click URL**. The compact hint is the thing agents copy verbatim, so the correlation token can ride inside it.

## The design

Search already mints the `search_id` and knows each hit's rank. Embed both in the per-hit hint:

```json
{
  "id": "REDACTED",
  "title": "Elect a single checkpoint sync remote...",
  "score": 0.91,
  "explain": "entire checkpoint explain REDACTED --search-id REDACTED:1"
}
```

`explain` gains one hidden, optional flag: `--search-id <ulid>[:<rank>]`. It changes nothing about resolution — it's passed straight through into the event:

```json
{
  "event": "cli_checkpoint_explained",
  "properties": {
    "checkpoint_id": "REDACTED",
    "source": "prose",
    "search_id": "REDACTED",
    "rank": 1
  }
}
```

Now the PostHog join is exact — `cli_search_performed.search_id == cli_checkpoint_explained.search_id` — no time-window heuristics, and you get **CTR-by-rank client-side**, which the stateless design previously couldn't measure at all. This is precisely how web search does it: the SERP link carries the tracking params; the click is deterministic because the server wrote the URL.

## Why this beats the alternatives

- **Local impression store** — deterministic, but it's the stateful design you already rejected (files under `.git/`, TTL bookkeeping).
- **Server-side impression logging in query-serve** — also deterministic and immune to agent behavior, but it's a cross-repo lift and puts the join in warehouse/Datadog instead of one PostHog dashboard. Still the right *eventual* home for full impression sets; the envelope `search_id` remains the seam for it.
- **This** — ~45 extra characters per hit and one hidden flag. That's the whole cost.

## The honest caveat

Determinism holds only when the agent copies the hint verbatim. The original discussion worried agents would drop a flag they had to *construct* — but here they only have to *not delete* it from a ready-made command, which is the high-probability path. When they do strip it (or a human types the id by hand), the event simply lacks `search_id` and you fall back to today's time-window correlation. Usefully, that failure mode is itself measurable: the fraction of `cli_checkpoint_explained` events carrying `search_id` tells you hint compliance directly, per agent version.

One privacy note: both values are opaque ULIDs/small ints, so nothing new leaves the machine — this stays inside the posture we documented.

Want me to implement it? It's small: extend `explainHint` to append the token, add the hidden flag to `explain` (threaded to the three emit sites), include `search_id`/`rank` in the event when present, plus tests and a doc line — and I'd note the update on ENT-1528.

git status --short && git add cmd/entire/cli/telemetry/search.go cmd/entire/cli/telemetry/search_test.go cmd/entire/cli/search_telemetry.go cmd/entire/cli/search_telemetry_test.go cmd/entire/cli/search_cmd.go cmd/entire/cli/search_cmd_test.go cmd/entire/cli/explain.go docs/security-and-privacy.md && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(search): deterministic search→explain attribution via hint token

Time-proximity correlation can't prove an explained checkpoint came from
a search. Since the CLI authors the click command, embed the link in it:
compact hints now end with --search-id <search_id>:<rank>, and explain
gains that hidden flag, threading the validated token through the
context (same pattern as withCrossRepoRead) into cli_checkpoint_explained
as search_id + rank. The PostHog funnel joins exactly on search_id and
gets CTR-by-rank client-side; token-less explains still fall back to
time-window correlation, and their share measures hint compliance.

The flag value is agent-controlled text, so it is strictly validated
(26-char ULID, positive rank) and silently dropped when malformed —
attribution metadata must never fail an explain or leak junk into
telemetry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push 2>&1 | tail -2
